f.title: Breach report to the Commissioner: in writing, with circumstances and cause, date or period, and information affected
f.statement: A report of a breach of security safeguards to the Privacy Commissioner under PIPEDA s. 10.1(2) must be in writing and must contain (a) a description of the circumstances of the breach and, if known, the cause; (b) the day on which, or the period during which, the breach occurred or, if neither is known, the approximate period; and (c) a description of the personal information that is the subject of the breach to the extent that the information is known. Items (d) to (g) are the next rows.
f.clause: s. 2(1)(a)-(c) Report — content, form and manner
f.applicability: Breaches of security safeguards involving personal information under the control of an organization subject to PIPEDA Part 1 (PIPEDA ss. 10.1 and 10.3). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects.
f.exceptions: Timing is set by PIPEDA s. 10.1(2): as soon as feasible after the organization determines that the breach has occurred (no fixed number).

f.title: Breach report: number of individuals affected and mitigation steps taken
f.statement: The breach report under s. 2(1) must also contain (d) the number of individuals affected by the breach or, if unknown, the approximate number; and (e) a description of the steps that the organization has taken to reduce the risk of harm to affected individuals that could result from the breach or to mitigate that harm.

f.title: Breach report: steps to notify individuals and a contact person for the Commissioner
f.statement: The breach report under s. 2(1) must also contain (f) a description of the steps that the organization has taken or intends to take to notify affected individuals of the breach in accordance with PIPEDA s. 10.1(3); and (g) the name and contact information of a person who can answer, on behalf of the organization, the Commissioner's questions about the breach.

f.statement: An organization may submit to the Commissioner any new information referred to in s. 2(1) that it becomes aware of after having made the report.
f.applicability: Breaches of security safeguards involving personal information under the control of an organization subject to PIPEDA Part 1 (PIPEDA ss. 10.1 and 10.3). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects.

f.title: Notice to affected individuals: circumstances, date or period, and information affected
f.statement: A notification provided by an organization to an affected individual under PIPEDA s. 10.1(3) must contain (a) a description of the circumstances of the breach; (b) the day on which, or period during which, the breach occurred or, if neither is known, the approximate period; and (c) a description of the personal information that is the subject of the breach to the extent that the information is known. Items (d) to (f) are the next row.
f.applicability: Breaches of security safeguards involving personal information under the control of an organization subject to PIPEDA Part 1 (PIPEDA ss. 10.1 and 10.3). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects.
f.exceptions: Timing is set by PIPEDA s. 10.1(6): as soon as feasible after the organization determines that the breach has occurred.

f.title: Notice to affected individuals: mitigation steps, steps individuals can take, and contact information
f.statement: The notification to an affected individual must also contain (d) a description of the steps that the organization has taken to reduce the risk of harm that could result from the breach; (e) a description of the steps that affected individuals could take to reduce the risk of harm that could result from the breach or to mitigate that harm; and (f) contact information that the affected individual can use to obtain further information about the breach.
f.applicability: Breaches of security safeguards involving personal information under the control of an organization subject to PIPEDA Part 1 (PIPEDA ss. 10.1 and 10.3). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects.

f.title: Give direct notice in person, by telephone, mail, email or other reasonable means
f.statement: For PIPEDA s. 10.1(5), direct notification must be given to the affected individual in person, by telephone, mail, email or any other form of communication that a reasonable person would consider appropriate in the circumstances.

f.title: Use indirect notice when direct notice would cause further harm or undue hardship, or contact details are lacking
f.statement: For PIPEDA s. 10.1(5), indirect notification must be given by an organization in any of the following circumstances: (a) direct notification would be likely to cause further harm to the affected individual; (b) direct notification would be likely to cause undue hardship for the organization; or (c) the organization does not have contact information for the affected individual.

f.statement: For PIPEDA s. 10.1(5), indirect notification must be given by public communication or a similar measure that could reasonably be expected to reach the affected individuals.

f.title: Keep a record of every breach for 24 months after determining that it occurred
f.statement: For PIPEDA s. 10.3(1), an organization must maintain a record of every breach of security safeguards for 24 months after the day on which the organization determines that the breach has occurred.
f.applicability: Breaches of security safeguards involving personal information under the control of an organization subject to PIPEDA Part 1 (PIPEDA ss. 10.1 and 10.3). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects.

f.title: Breach record must contain enough information for the Commissioner to verify compliance with s. 10.1(1) and (3)
f.statement: The record referred to in PIPEDA s. 10.3(1) must contain any information that enables the Commissioner to verify compliance with PIPEDA s. 10.1(1) (reporting to the Commissioner) and s. 10.1(3) (notifying individuals).
f.applicability: Breaches of security safeguards involving personal information under the control of an organization subject to PIPEDA Part 1 (PIPEDA ss. 10.1 and 10.3). The text draws no distinction between domestic and foreign data subjects.
